subject: Design partners wanted: Route-level A/B testing in Redwood Console (beta in Feb)
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@acmeai.com>, Priya Shah <priya@lexiflow.ai>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@finsight.io>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 29, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Design partners wanted: Route-level A/B testing in Redwood Console (beta in Feb)

Hi Alex / Priya / Ben,

We’re recruiting a small set of design partners for a new Console-first feature: **Route-level A/B testing**.

The goal is to let you split production traffic for a specific API route (e.g., /v1/chat/completions for a given project) across two model variants and compare **latency, cost, error rates**, and (optionally) **quality** using our eval harness.

What we’re looking for (design partner expectations):
- 1–2 routes where you can safely run an A/B split (typical: 90/10 → 50/50)
- Weekly 20-min check-in during the beta window
- Willingness to share “did this work / what’s missing?” feedback on:
  - experiment setup flow (create/validate/start/stop/rollback)
  - reporting (latency/TTFT, p95/p99, errors/timeouts, token & GPU cost attribution)
  - guardrails (alerts + rollback triggers)

Telemetry we need enabled (so results are trustworthy):
- Exposure logging from the gateway (experiment_id + variant)
- Ability to compute:
  - end-to-end latency + time-to-first-token
  - request/stream error rates (incl. 429s/timeouts)
  - prompt/completion token counts
  - per-request cost attribution (token + GPU)
- A stable stickiness key for deterministic assignment (more below). No PII required.

Stickiness / assignment (high level):
- We bucket deterministically using a hash of stable identifiers available at the gateway.
- Recommended: provide a stable user/session identifier header (we’ll share exact header name + format).
- If you don’t have that available, we can fall back to api_key_id / tenant-level stickiness (with some tradeoffs).

Proposed timeline (beta):
- Week of **Feb 17**: beta flag enablement for design partners + onboarding
- Feb 17 – Mar 6: experiment setup + internal validation
- Mar 9 – Apr 3: run experiment(s) + iterate on reporting/guardrails

If you’re interested, can you reply with:
1) Which deployment you’re on today (Hosted API vs Dedicated)
2) Which route(s) you’d want to test
3) Whether you can pass a stable user/session identifier header at request time

Attachment: a short overview + what we’ll ask you to validate.

Thanks,
Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Route_AB_Testing_Beta_Overview_2026-01-29.pdf
Attachment: Telemetry_Requirements_AB_Testing_Beta_v1.txt



From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 30, 2026 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Design partners wanted: Route-level A/B testing in Redwood Console (beta in Feb)

Hi Marissa,

Interested. We’ve been hacking this ourselves and it’s painful to get apples-to-apples cost + TTFT.

Quick questions:
1) We’re on Dedicated (us-east + eu-west). Is the beta supported there?
2) On the stickiness key: we can pass a user id, but our legal/security folks will ask about PII. Is it stored anywhere?
3) Any guidance on retention for exposure logs / experiment events?

Routes: /v1/chat/completions (primary) and possibly embeddings.

Thanks,
Alex



From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@acmeai.com>, Priya Shah <priya@lexiflow.ai>, Ben Torres <ben.torres@finsight.io>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 30, 2026 at 12:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: Design partners wanted: Route-level A/B testing in Redwood Console (beta in Feb)

Alex (and all) — great, thanks.

Answers:
1) **Dedicated support:** Yes. Beta is planned for Hosted + Dedicated. Private/VPC/on-prem is likely follow-on.
2) **PII:** You do not need to send raw user identifiers. The preferred approach is to send a stable, opaque identifier (or a one-way hash on your side). On our side we treat it as an assignment input only.
   - Exposure events do **not** include prompt text.
   - We are explicitly avoiding high-cardinality user-level dimensions in metrics.
3) **Retention:** For beta we’re planning a shorter retention window for raw exposure events (target: 14–30 days) and longer retention for aggregated metrics in Console. We can share the exact numbers once we finalize with Security/SRE.

On stickiness header: we’ll follow up with the exact header spec once the gateway allowlist is locked (we’re trying to keep it very small to avoid cardinality surprises).

If helpful, we can also default to api_key_id stickiness for initial validation and then move to per-user/session once you’re comfortable.

Next step: if you’re up for it, I’d like to schedule a 30-min kickoff the week of Feb 10 to confirm routes, regions, and guardrail thresholds.

Marissa

From: Ben Torres <ben.torres@finsight.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 2, 2026 at 3:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: Design partners wanted: Route-level A/B testing in Redwood Console (beta in Feb)

Marissa,

We’re interested as well (Hosted API today, may move to Dedicated later this quarter).

One question: on the optional quality measurement, are you expecting online human/LLM judging or just offline eval suites? We can provide a prompt set + expected rubric, but we’re sensitive to anything that requires shipping production data out of band.

Also: do you provide any guidance in the UI about sample size / confidence? We’ve had internal debates where people read too much into small deltas.

Ben



From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Torres <ben.torres@finsight.io>, Alex Kim <alex.kim@acmeai.com>, Priya Shah <priya@lexiflow.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 4:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: Design partners wanted: Route-level A/B testing in Redwood Console (beta in Feb)

Ben — yes, totally aligned on avoiding anything that feels like “ship prod data somewhere else.”

For v1 beta:
- **Quality is optional and offline-first.** You can attach an eval suite / prompt set to the experiment and run it against the same two variants/configs.
- We are **not** requiring online judge sampling as part of the design partner program (we’re likely deferring that until after GA).

On stats/confidence:
- The results dashboard will show deltas with a confidence indicator and guard against misleading reads at low exposure volume.
- We’ll also surface basic “minimum sample size” guidance (we’re still tuning exact copy).

Operationally, the primary success criteria for the beta is that you can:
1) set up the experiment safely,
2) trust latency/cost/error reporting, and
3) stop/rollback quickly with clear auditability.

If you (or your team) can share which two variants you’d want to compare (model name + any special config like max tokens/temperature), that helps us prep enablement.

I’ll send a separate note with a few kickoff slots.

Best,
Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference
